terms.definition: The number of consecutive Dry seasons (z below −0.5) ending with a given season when all MAM and OND seasons are walked in strict chronological order. Any Normal, Wet or missing season resets the count to zero. The longest run in a county record and its cumulative rainfall deficit summarise multi-season drought persistence.
terms.tooltip: The number of consecutive Dry seasons (z below −0.5) ending with a given season when all MAM and OND seasons are walked in strict chronological order.
terms.canonical_reference: Kenya ENSO Explorer methods monograph, Figure 3.1B.

terms.definition: A strictly proper scoring rule for probabilistic forecasts of ordered categories, equal to the sum of squared differences between the cumulative forecast probabilities and the cumulative observation indicator over the categories. For three rainfall terciles only the first two cumulative terms are informative. Forecasts that place probability far from the observed category are penalised more than near misses.
terms.tooltip: A strictly proper scoring rule for probabilistic forecasts of ordered categories, equal to the sum of squared differences between the cumulative forecast probabilities and the cumulative observation indicator over the categories.
terms.canonical_reference: Epstein, E. S. (1969). A scoring system for probability forecasts of ranked categories. Journal of Applied Meteorology, 8(6), 985–987.

terms.definition: A categorical skill score that rescales the proportion of correct modal forecasts by the proportion expected from an uninformed forecast. For three equiprobable terciles the expected proportion is one third; HSS is 1 for perfect categorical forecasts, 0 for chance and negative for worse than chance.
terms.tooltip: A categorical skill score that rescales the proportion of correct modal forecasts by the proportion expected from an uninformed forecast.
terms.canonical_reference: Wilks, D. S. (2011). Statistical Methods in the Atmospheric Sciences (3rd ed.). Academic Press.

terms.definition: The skill of a probability forecast for one binary event (for example, the Dry tercile occurs) relative to the climatological probability, computed as one minus the ratio of the mean squared forecast error to the mean squared climatological error. The Explorer reports BSS separately for the drought-relevant Dry tercile and the flood-relevant Wet tercile.
terms.tooltip: The skill of a probability forecast for one binary event (for example, the Dry tercile occurs) relative to the climatological probability, computed as one minus the ratio of the mean squared forecast error to the mean squared climatological error.
terms.canonical_reference: Wilks, D. S. (2011). Statistical Methods in the Atmospheric Sciences (3rd ed.). Academic Press.

terms.definition: The improvement of a forecast system over a reference forecast, measured here by the leave-one-out cross-validated Ranked Probability Skill Score against equal-odds climatology and labelled High (RPSS at least 0.20), Moderate (0.10 to 0.20), Marginal (0 to 0.10) or No skill (below 0). The class sets the colour of the skill badge and the guidance text beside each outlook; probabilities are displayed in every class, so a No-skill outlook should be read as a historical frequency only.
terms.tooltip: The improvement of a forecast system over a reference forecast, measured here by the leave-one-out cross-validated Ranked Probability Skill Score against equal-odds climatology and labelled High (RPSS at least 0.20), Moderate (0.10 to 0.20), Marginal (0 to 0.10) or No skill (below 0).
terms.canonical_reference: Jolliffe, I. T., & Stephenson, D. B. (Eds.). (2012). Forecast Verification: A Practitioner's Guide in Atmospheric Science (2nd ed.). Wiley.

terms.definition: The replacement value of the live herd in a county, computed as head count times a capital-share adjustment for herd structure times the county sale price (0.75 of the mature sale price for cattle, goats and sheep; a species-specific herd-structure ratio for camels). It is a stock, distinct from the annual flow of offtake and milk, and is the quantity that drought mortality and distress sales erode.
terms.tooltip: The replacement value of the live herd in a county, computed as head count times a capital-share adjustment for herd structure times the county sale price (0.75 of the mature sale price for cattle, goats and sheep; a species-specific herd-structure ratio for camels).
terms.canonical_reference: Behnke, R., & Muthami, D. (2011). The contribution of livestock to the Kenyan economy. IGAD LPI Working Paper 03-11.

terms.definition: Commodity-specific, mass-preserving weights that distribute each statutory county valuation total across the 290 IEBC parliamentary constituencies: MapSPAM 2020 physical crop area for crops and 2019 census household livestock counts for livestock and products, with land-area shares as a flagged fallback where the prior is zero. Shares sum to one within each county and commodity, so constituency values re-aggregate exactly to the county total.
terms.tooltip: Commodity-specific, mass-preserving weights that distribute each statutory county valuation total across the 290 IEBC parliamentary constituencies: MapSPAM 2020 physical crop area for crops and 2019 census household livestock counts for livestock and products, with land-area shares as a flagged fallback where the prior is zero.
terms.formula_or_metric: w_{sc} = \frac{A_{sc}}{\sum_{k \in c} A_{k}}, \quad \sum_{sc \in c} w_{sc} = 1, \quad V_{sc} = w_{sc} V_c
terms.canonical_reference: Kenya ENSO Explorer methods monograph, Figure 1.2.

terms.definition: The publication posture applied to the Section 1.2 economic valuation assets while formal licensing of the National Drought Management Authority bulletin prices is sought: values are shown for expert review as modeled screening estimates, carry a Beta Review Edition banner, provide no bulk download, and are excluded from the open Atlas data store and the Comprehensive Data Hub. The figures are not calibrated for direct use in fiscal transfers or compensation.
terms.tooltip: The publication posture applied to the Section 1.2 economic valuation assets while formal licensing of the National Drought Management Authority bulletin prices is sought: values are shown for expert review as modeled screening estimates, carry a Beta Review Edition banner, provide no bulk download, and are excluded from the open Atlas data store and the Comprehensive Data Hub.
terms.canonical_reference: National Drought Management Authority County Drought Early Warning Bulletins (2019–2021), used under research fair dealing.

terms.definition: A historical season whose equatorial ocean state most closely resembles the current or forecast state, selected by the smallest standardized Euclidean distance in Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) and Dipole Mode Index (DMI) space. The rainfall terciles observed in the k nearest analogue years (k = 5 or 8) give the empirical outlook probabilities.
terms.tooltip: A historical season whose equatorial ocean state most closely resembles the current or forecast state, selected by the smallest standardized Euclidean distance in Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) and Dipole Mode Index (DMI) space.
terms.formula_or_metric: \mathcal{A} = \{k \text{ years with smallest } D_{i} \}, \quad D_i = \sqrt{\textstyle\sum_d (\Delta x_{i,d}/\sigma_d)^2}
terms.canonical_reference: Kenya ENSO Explorer methods monograph, Table 2.3 (forecast verification).

terms.definition: The combined classification of a season by its ENSO phase and its Indian Ocean Dipole phase. ENSO phase is El Niño when the seasonal-mean Relative Oceanic Niño Index exceeds +0.5 °C, La Niña below -0.5 °C, and Neutral otherwise; IOD phase is positive when the October to December mean Dipole Mode Index exceeds +0.4 °C, negative below -0.4 °C, and neutral otherwise.
terms.tooltip: The combined classification of a season by its ENSO phase and its Indian Ocean Dipole phase.
terms.canonical_reference: Saji, N. H., Goswami, B. N., Vinayachandran, P. N., & Yamagata, T. (1999). A dipole mode in the tropical Indian Ocean. Nature, 401, 360-363.

terms.definition: The empirical probability that seasonal rainfall falls in the Drier, Near normal or Wetter tercile given a stated ocean condition, estimated as the relative frequency of each tercile among historical seasons that share that condition. It is compared with the unconditioned climatological probability of one third.
terms.tooltip: The empirical probability that seasonal rainfall falls in the Drier, Near normal or Wetter tercile given a stated ocean condition, estimated as the relative frequency of each tercile among historical seasons that share that condition.
terms.canonical_reference: Wilks, D. S. (2011). Statistical Methods in the Atmospheric Sciences (3rd ed.). Academic Press.

terms.definition: A cross-tabulation of counts between two categorical variables, used here to tabulate ocean phase against observed rainfall tercile and, in forecast verification, the predicted modal tercile against the observed tercile. Row-normalized cells give conditional frequencies.
terms.tooltip: A cross-tabulation of counts between two categorical variables, used here to tabulate ocean phase against observed rainfall tercile and, in forecast verification, the predicted modal tercile against the observed tercile.
terms.formula_or_metric: n_{ij} = \#\{y : A_y = i,\ B_y = j\}, \quad \hat{P}(B = j \mid A = i) = n_{ij} / n_{i\cdot}
terms.canonical_reference: Jolliffe, I. T., & Stephenson, D. B. (Eds.). (2012). Forecast Verification: A Practitioner's Guide in Atmospheric Science (2nd ed.). Wiley.

terms.definition: The residual of a crop production or yield series from its fitted linear time trend, expressed in absolute units and as a percentage of the trend value. Removing the trend separates year-to-year climate shocks from long-run changes in area, technology and reporting.
terms.tooltip: The residual of a crop production or yield series from its fitted linear time trend, expressed in absolute units and as a percentage of the trend value.
terms.formula_or_metric: a_y = Y_y - (\hat\beta_0 + \hat\beta_1 y), \qquad a_y^{\%} = 100\, a_y / (\hat\beta_0 + \hat\beta_1 y)
terms.canonical_reference: Lobell, D. B., & Field, C. B. (2007). Global scale climate-crop yield relationships and the impacts of recent warming. Environmental Research Letters, 2(1), 014002.

terms.definition: The official drought early warning stage assigned to each arid and semi-arid county in the National Drought Management Authority monthly bulletins: Normal, Alert, Alarm, Emergency, and Recovery. Stages combine biophysical indicators (rainfall, vegetation condition, water) with livelihood indicators (livestock condition, prices, nutrition) and trigger contingency financing.
terms.tooltip: The official drought early warning stage assigned to each arid and semi-arid county in the National Drought Management Authority monthly bulletins: Normal, Alert, Alarm, Emergency, and Recovery.
terms.canonical_reference: National Drought Management Authority (NDMA). County Drought Early Warning Bulletins. Nairobi: NDMA.

terms.definition: An international XML standard (OASIS CAP 1.2) for exchanging public warnings across media. The Kenya Meteorological Department publishes its severe weather warnings as a machine-readable CAP feed, which the Explorer reads to list current and recent advisories by county.
terms.tooltip: An international XML standard (OASIS CAP 1.2) for exchanging public warnings across media.
terms.canonical_reference: OASIS (2010). Common Alerting Protocol Version 1.2. OASIS Standard.

terms.definition: The zonal overturning circulation of the tropical atmosphere, with rising air over the warm western Pacific and Maritime Continent and sinking air over the eastern Pacific, and a corresponding Indian Ocean cell. ENSO and the Indian Ocean Dipole shift these cells, changing subsidence and moisture convergence over East Africa and so modulating the Short Rains.
terms.tooltip: The zonal overturning circulation of the tropical atmosphere, with rising air over the warm western Pacific and Maritime Continent and sinking air over the eastern Pacific, and a corresponding Indian Ocean cell.
terms.canonical_reference: Nicholson, S. E. (2017). Climate and climatic variability of rainfall over eastern Africa. Reviews of Geophysics, 55(3), 590-635.
